transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-06-09 16:00 UTC
Duration: 46 min
Attendees: Sophie Nguyen (Redwood AE); Mateo Rivera (Redwood SE); Priya Kapoor (DeltaForge - Dir IT Sec); Ethan Long (DeltaForge - ML Eng); Marco Silva (DeltaForge - DevOps); Aisha Rahman (DeltaForge - PO)

Summary:
Quick weekly POC sync focusing on security/compliance gating items: SSO/SAML, audit log retention/format, SOC 2 evidence for pilot, and next steps for latency/cost tuning. Agreed to a small audit log export and clarifications on retention policy.

Topics: SSO Integration; Audit Logs & Retention; SOC 2 controls mapping; Pilot runtime tuning (latency/cost); Next steps

[00:00] Sophie Nguyen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining on short notice, we'll keep it tight, 45 minutes ish. Quick roll call?
[00:08] Priya Kapoor: Priya here.
[00:09] Ethan Long: Ethan.
[00:10] Marco Silva: Marco.
[00:11] Aisha Rahman: Aisha.
[00:12] Mateo Rivera: Mateo from Redwood.
[00:14] Sophie Nguyen: Great. Agenda — pick up on the SSO integration status, audit logs, and SOC 2 evidence requests, then tuning notes from Mateo's run last week.

[02:05] Priya Kapoor: On SSO we did a test with our IdP and saw the SAML assertion mapping issue — username attribute didn't map to email, so user provisioning for the console failed.
[02:22] Marco Silva: Yeah the redirect URI was also blocked by our CSP until we added the call.
[02:30] Sophie Nguyen: Right, thanks. Mateo, can you share the minor change we pushed to metadata to accept NameID/email alias?
[02:45] Mateo Rivera: Sure, we updated the SP metadata to accept mail and emailAddress attributes, and added a fallback to NameID when present. There was a small mis-sample in the IdP where the attribute name was 'mail' not 'email' which caused the fail.
[03:18] Ethan Long: transcription note — the console shows SS-Oh errors for a sec, then comes back.
[03:27] Sophie Nguyen: (laugh) we've seen that, yeah. Priya, once you update the attribute mapping on your side it should be green. Also we'll send a short step-by-step.

[05:00] Priya Kapoor: Another SSO ask — we need SAML assertions to be logged to our SIEM for audit, can you confirm Redwood can emit the assertion ID and subject in audit logs?
[05:15] Mateo Rivera: We log authentication events with a correlation id, we can add assertion id and subject email to the auth event. We'll provide a sample line. Note: we don't store full assertion payloads in logs by default for PII reasons.
[05:41] Priya Kapoor: Ok that's acceptable, as long as the ID is present and we can correlate to our SIEM. Do you support syslog or do we need to pull logs via API?
[05:52] Mateo Rivera: Currently push to S3 (secure bucket) and API pull; syslog forwarder not supported in hosted pilot, but we can emulate push to your S3 indexer or provide a CloudWatch/Stackdriver sink depending on region.

[07:10] Aisha Rahman: For the pilot we're trying to prove 30 day retention is fine, but legal might ask for 90. Priya, any update?
[07:20] Priya Kapoor: We're evaluating. For now I'm asking legal to confirm whether auth/audit logs must be 90 days for our vertical. I'll get back by next Monday.

[08:40] Mateo Rivera: On audit logs format — we'll include event timestamp, user id/email, action (login, token issue, model call), correlation id, assertion id (if available), and truncated request id (first 8 chars). Sample schema will be sent.

[10:05] Marco Silva: We need logs to be redact-friendly — PII removal, and ability to request a TTL-based purge for a specific customer or user.
[10:20] Mateo Rivera: We have TTL-based retention jobs; for the pilot we can run a manual purge script if you need one-off removal. For the product we'll expose a retention policy endpoint (RBAC gated).

[12:00] Sophie Nguyen: On SOC 2 — Priya, you shared the initial control matrix last week. Two gaps we flagged: artifact-level evidence for encryption at rest using customer KMS, and periodic vulnerability scans of the pilot environment.
[12:22] Priya Kapoor: Yes, we need to see KMS integration proof and also EDR logs on the host for the pilot nodes.
[12:35] Mateo Rivera: For KMS, in Redwood Private we integrate with customer KMS via IAM roles and key policies; for the hosted pilot we used a demo KMS but we can show the config diff and steps; we can also provide a proof-of-configuration doc and a snippet of the test encryption key rotation.
[13:05] Sophie Nguyen: We'll upload that to the shared drive — Sophie will do that by Friday.

[14:10] Ethan Long: Quick question on data in transit vs at rest: will model KV caches ever be persisted to disk in a way that could contain PII?
[14:25] Mateo Rivera: Good question. By default KV cache is in-memory on the inference pods, not persisted. There are optional spill-to-disk paths for very long context runs — not enabled in this pilot. We'll make sure settings are disabled and document the runtime flags. If you want, we can test a run with synthetic PII and show it never touches disk.
[15:05] Priya Kapoor: Please do that test, we need that assurance.

[16:30] Marco Silva: About network topology — we need VPC peering details and the ip ranges for the pilot cluster. Also firewall rules for control-plane callbacks.
[16:45] Sophie Nguyen: We'll share a minimal allowlist doc. Marco, can you share the subnets you plan to peer?
[16:52] Marco Silva: I'll push the subnets to the ticket after this call.

[18:00] Mateo Rivera: On performance tuning — we ran the 2-hour latency run last night. Average 95th percentile token latency was ~230ms for 2k token contexts on the current dedicated pool. When we reduced batch size it dropped to ~160ms but cost per token increased ~12%. So there's a tradeoff.
[18:28] Ethan Long: That's helpful. For our app 200ms is ok but cost is a hard limit. Do you have quantization options?
[18:38] Mateo Rivera: Yes we've tested an INT8 path; quality delta was small on your sample prompts, cost improvement ~30%, but inference latency increased slightly due to dequant/dequant ops for long sequences. We'll send the eval doc with ROUGE/QA scores.

[20:10] Aisha Rahman: Also, are there any auto-scaling gaps that might affect audit continuity? If a pod spins up mid-flight, do logs reconnect to the same correlation id?
[20:26] Mateo Rivera: We generate a request correlation id at the proxy layer and pass it through; autoscaling just adds more consumers but the correlation id persists across retries. We will include a diagram of the flow.

[22:00] Priya Kapoor: Back to SOC 2 — we need an ISSUED date on your last penetration test and the scope. Is that public?
[22:12] Sophie Nguyen: We can share the redacted pentest summary and date — last was 2027-04-02, scope included control plane and edge services (non-prod excluded). We'll add the redaction and link.

[24:10] Marco Silva: For retention, if we choose 30 days, can we get a weekly export snapshot so our SIEM ingests it?
[24:25] Mateo Rivera: Yes, we can schedule daily or weekly exports to your S3. We'll provide a small lambda example to ingest into your SIEM.

[26:40] Ethan Long: One minor transcription hiccup — the engine name in the logs was written as 'Redwood serv' in the demo clip.
[26:48] Sophie Nguyen: That's likely an artifact of the demo config; we'll standardize naming conventions in the sample logs.

[28:10] Priya Kapoor: I'd like to summarize gating criteria for pilot to move to enterprise: 1) SSO stable with assertion id in logs, 2) confirmed retention policy + purge capability, 3) KMS evidence or documented plan, 4) redacted pentest summary received. Anything to add?
[28:30] Marco Silva: Also VPC peering and firewall cookbook.
[28:34] Aisha Rahman: And cost/runbook for token pricing at expected QPS.

[30:00] Sophie Nguyen: Good list. We'll treat those as the must-haves. Sophie will upload SOC 2 mapping and pentest summary; Mateo will deliver log samples and retention script; Marco will send VPC details; Priya will confirm retention window.

[32:15] Mateo Rivera: Quick demo note — the audit-log export I'll produce will be anonymized but with stable correlation ids so you can validate the pipeline. Expect a ~50MB gz file for a 24h sample.

[33:40] Ethan Long: On the performance side, can we try one run with INT8 and a 512 token cap to compare latency/cost?
[33:50] Mateo Rivera: Yes, we'll run that as a follow-up and include the eval notebook.

[35:10] Priya Kapoor: One compliance nuance — our internal policy forbids storing assertion payloads longer than X seconds, so having the assertion id in logs is enough, but not the full assertion. Confirmed?
[35:25] Mateo Rivera: Confirmed, we will not log full assertion payloads and will only store the metadata fields we discussed.

[36:40] Marco Silva: About RBAC — can we map roles to our SSO groups so developers don't get admin console rights by default?
[36:50] Sophie Nguyen: Yes, we support group-to-role mapping, and default roles can be set at the org level. We'll send a small JSON mapping example.

[38:10] Aisha Rahman: Any blockers we should be aware of?
[38:15] Priya Kapoor: Just the legal retention clarification and a final check on KMS.
[38:20] Marco Silva: For networking I need the allowlist doc.

[39:00] Sophie Nguyen: Quick recap of next steps then — we'll share three artifacts: SOC 2 mapping + redacted pentest, sample audit-log export + schema, and SSO step-by-step plus group-role mapping examples. Customer sends retention decision and network details.

[40:10] Mateo Rivera: I'll queue the 24h audit export and the INT8 run; expect both by Monday/Tuesday.

[41:30] Priya Kapoor: If we get the KMS evidence and the logs, we can fast-track a security sign-off for pilot extension.

[42:10] Sophie Nguyen: Perfect. We'll also attach the cost tradeoff spreadsheet for the INT8 vs baseline runs.

[43:50] Ethan Long: minor cross talk — thanks all, tldr: SSO mapping fix, log samples, KMS proof, retention window decision.
[44:05] Sophie Nguyen: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up in the CRM and Slack channel.
[44:15] Marco Silva: Thanks.
[44:18] Aisha Rahman: Thank you.
[44:20] Meeting end.

References and links mentioned:
- SOC 2 partial control mapping (to be uploaded to shared drive)
- Sample audit-log export (s3 link to be provided by Mateo)
- Allowlist & network cookbook (Sophie to upload)
- INT8 evaluation notebook (linked in follow-up email)

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-heard acronyms (SS-Oh for SSO), some proper nouns may be slightly off (Redwood serv) — verified by attendees during call.
